title: Agentic AI Governance Dimension for the FLI Safety Index

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: agentic AI governance is a timely and critical gap. Designing indicators based on existing frameworks (Singapore IMDA, NIST) and scoring companies provides immediately useful governance data.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Intermediate: designing 6-8 governance indicators from scratch requires domain knowledge of both agentic AI systems and governance methodology. Beginners would need heavy guidance.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Sustained effort: designing indicators, operationalizing them, and scoring 8 companies. Feasible within 30 hours if indicators are kept simple, but risk of scope creep.

novelty.reasoning: The 2025 AI Agent Index from MIT (arXiv:2602.17753) already documents governance and safety features of 30 deployed agentic AI systems across six categories including safety/evaluation, autonomy/control, and ecosystem interaction. It found that only 15/30 agents have published safety frameworks, 25/30 disclose no internal safety results, and 23/30 have no third-party testing. Additionally, the FLI AI Safety Index Summer 2025 already evaluates companies on 33 indicators across six domains. The specific contribution of designing 6-8 agentic governance indicators and scoring companies is largely subsumed by these two existing indices. The remaining gap is a formal integration of agentic-specific indicators into the FLI methodology, but the empirical groundwork is done.

FLI AI Safety Index.details: Confirmed at futureoflife.org. Multiple editions (2024, Winter 2025, Summer 2025) evaluating frontier AI companies on 33 indicators across six domains.

2025 AI Agent Index (MIT).details: Confirmed via arXiv:2602.17753 and aiagentindex.mit.edu. Directly covers agentic AI governance indicators for 30 deployed systems.

Singapore IMDA AI Governance Framework.details: Singapore's IMDA has published AI governance frameworks. Relevant as a reference for designing governance indicators.
